transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Carlos Rivera (Horizon CTO), Priya Nair (Horizon Head of ML), Ben Thompson (Horizon Infra)

Summary (auto): Deep dive on Dedicated vs Hosted for latency and throughput guarantees. Focus areas: noisy neighbor isolation, KV cache sharing and prefix caching, batching strategies, quantization trade-offs, VPC/on-prem constraints and expected SLA for Dedicated pools. Action items and benchmark plan agreed.

Topics: runtime performance, latency/throughput, KV cache, batching, quantization, VPC/on-prem, isolation/noisy-neighbor, throughput guarantees

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick intros i guess, i'm maya from redwood, arjun is our infra/serving engineer, lena helps on solutions side.
[00:07] Carlos: hi yeah carlos here, we're excited to understand how to keep predictable latency for our customer-facing assistant.
[00:12] Priya: and priya, we'll be driving the ML evals, main question is we see big p95 spikes under load.
[00:18] Arjun: yep, that's exactly what i want to dig into — differences between hosted vs dedicated for noisy neighbor isolation and how our runtime manages kv cache and batching.
[00:26] Ben: quick note on network — we need to know VPC reqs for private deployment, firewall rules, egress, that sort of thing.
[00:31] Maya: great, agenda: 1) isolation/noisy-neighbor 2) throughput guarantees + autoscaling 3) caching & batching 4) quantization impacts 5) VPC/on-prem considerations and next steps. Sound good?
[00:40] Carlos: yes.

[00:45] Arjun: ok starting with isolation: in hosted mode you share our pool with multi-tenancy, we do soft isolation with cgroups and request shaping — works for most apps but you can see tail latency spikes if other tenants burst. in Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools so noisy neighbors are eliminated. dedicated also gives you blackout windows for maintenance, SLA-backed p99.
[01:05] Priya: what kind of p99 numbers do you commit to on Dedicated?
[01:08] Maya: our SLA tiers vary; for Dedicated we typically guarantee p99 latency within X% of baseline for configured seq lengths — i'll attach the SLA matrix, but ballpark for Llama-2 70B quantized models at 2k tokens it's in the low hundreds of milliseconds on our Dedicated X pools under expected throughput.
[01:27] Carlos: low hundreds p99 is fine but we need predictable throughput as well — we operate a bursty pattern with morning peak and then steady tail.

[01:33] Arjun: for throughput guarantees we provision Dedicated pools with a committed vGPU count and a configurable autoscaler. you can set zones for capacity and a burst bucket. when the pool exceeds commit, requests fall back to lower-cost variants or to hosted fallback policies based on your routing rules.
[01:48] Ben: is there noisy neighbor inside a Dedicated pool if multiple teams from our org are on same pool?
[01:52] Arjun: you can either have a single-tenant Dedicated pool or multiple namespaces with isolation via runtime tenancy. single-tenant ensures absolute isolation; multi-namespace gives flexible utilization but we can still apply QoS.

[02:02] [timestamp glitch] Speaker 4: mm-hmm

[02:10] Arjun: KV cache — key point: our KV cache is per-model-instance and we support prefix caching at request router; in hosted mode cache entries may be evicted more aggressively due to overall memory pressure. Dedicated pools let you size KV cache and preserve long-lived sessions, which improves p95/p99 for long convo flows.
[02:33] Priya: does the KV cache persist across restarts or rollouts?
[02:36] Arjun: by default KV is in-memory, but our rollout flow includes warm-up strategies: we can pre-warm common prefixes, and in Dedicated you get longer-lived workers so restarts are rarer. we also support a secondary LRU persistent cache option (optional add-on) that reduces cold start penalties.
[02:51] Carlos: any gotchas with sharded KV or cross-node consistency?
[02:54] Arjun: it's sharded per-worker; we keep sticky routing for a session to keep most of the KV local. on very high concurrency we do best-effort replication and that's where p99 can rise slightly if a session moves nodes. Dedicated reduces session churn.

[03:12] Maya: batching strategies — we do continuous batching inside the runtime; batch size and timeout parameters can be tuned. for latency sensitive paths we use micro-batching with very low timeouts; for high throughput non-interactive jobs you increase batch windows to maximize GPU utilization.
[03:32] Priya: will increased batching change response ordering or cost?
[03:35] Arjun: response ordering preserved per request; cost per token drops with larger batches. tradeoff is added queuing latency; our console surfaces token-level cost vs latency tradeoffs so you can choose.

[03:48] Ben: quantization — we saw some artifacts at 8-bit in evals, any guidance?
[03:52] Arjun: quantization depends on model family and prompts. we support 8-bit and 4-bit quant profiles; 8-bit often yields near-native quality for many workloads, 4-bit can reduce memory and improve throughput but might introduce occasional quality regressions. Redwood Optimize can run per-prompt recommendations and suggest switching quant profiles for defined prompt sets.
[04:12] Priya: can we A/B quant profiles in production safely?
[04:14] Maya: yes, rollouts support canary by route and we capture eval metrics and regressions tied to prompt sets. you can auto-fallback to a higher-quality variant if regression exceeds threshold.

[04:24] Carlos: what about VPC/on-prem — network latency to the model matters; do you support private control plane?
[04:29] Maya: for Private deployments we offer a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package. VPC peering or private link supported, and you can keep data paths inside your network. note: true on-prem adds ops overhead but gives max data residency and compliance.
[04:43] Ben: firewall ports? we have strict egress policies.
[04:46] Arjun: we will share a network doc but essentially you need outbound TLS to specific IP ranges or private link endpoints; we also support explicit proxying. we'll include the exact firewall table in the follow-up.

[04:58] Priya: security/compliance — we need SOC2 and audit logs. how fine-grained are the audit trails?
[05:02] Maya: audit logs are tokenized and show per-request metadata, model version, route, user id; for Private we can do longer retention and direct KMS integration. we'll attach SOC2 and ISO reports.

[05:13] Arjun: a few notes on behavior under contention: 1) prefix caching reduces work by avoiding repeated LM decoding, 2) continuous batching smooths spikes but can add 10s-100s ms if you increase batch windows, 3) Dedicated pools reduce variance but you should still define fallback routing to an alternate region or smaller model for resilience.
[05:35] Carlos: i'd like to see a benchmark with our exact prompts — p95 and p99, and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:40] Maya: agreed. action item: we'll run a 1-hour benchmark simulating your traffic with both Hosted baseline and Dedicated pool with same model and quant profiles.

[05:48] Arjun: for the benchmark i'll need your prompt set and sequence length distribution, and target concurrency windows. please include any long dialog contexts to exercise KV cache.
[05:58] Priya: i'll send that after the call.

[06:02] Ben: on contract terms, what's the minimum commit for Dedicated?
[06:05] Maya: we have a few tiers — small committed pools start at a monthly vGPU minimum (see pricing sheet). enterprise terms negotiable depending on region and support. i'll share the pricing sheet in the follow-up.

[06:16] Carlos: any limitations on model variants for Dedicated?
[06:19] Arjun: most open models we support; for very custom models we can onboard via private model upload with additional validation. quantization options vary by architecture.

[06:28] Priya: how do you handle model rollouts without killing KV cache?
[06:31] Arjun: we use rolling updates with sticky sessions and warm-up. for major blueprint changes we recommend canary traffic and pre-warming of common prefixes; Dedicated reduces frequency of worker churn which helps.

[06:45] [crosstalk] Maya: quick recap, we will: share SLA/pricing, run benchmark, provide security docs and network table, and schedule VPC onboarding if needed.
[06:55] Carlos: sounds good. let's aim for the follow-up in about a week.

[07:00] Maya: thanks all. end.
